accountNeeded: Slack workspace where you can create and install apps
agentCan: Draft scope lists for a feature
Draft redirect URLs and install links
approvalWait: None for installing in your own workspace. Public distribution and Slack Marketplace listing can add review time, which varies and is not published as a single fixed number.

blockers.fix: Compare the URL in the install link, the app settings, and your server route character by character.

blockers.blocker: Scope conflict with Sign in with Slack
blockers.fix: Split the flows. Do not combine Sign in with Slack user scopes with other scopes in one authorize request.

blockers.blocker: App works in your workspace but not in another
blockers.fix: Check distribution settings and whether the other workspace admin approved the install. A private test install does not prove public distribution works.

checklist.item: App name and workspace are correct
Redirect URL saved and matches the code exactly
Bot scopes and user scopes are separate and minimal
Client ID, client secret, and signing secret stored securely
Test install completed in a real workspace
Distribution description and support contact, for public use

difficultyWhy: Setup is quick, but distribution, workspace install rules, and scope choices make the full launch harder than a single workspace test.
humanMust: Create the app and pick the workspace
Install and approve scopes in Slack
Submit for public distribution if needed
managedAppNote: If a managed directory already covers Slack, use it for a first version. Register your own app when you need your own scopes, bot identity, or distribution.
name: Slack
nextStep: Create a blank Slack app in your development workspace, add your exact redirect URL, then install it and test one API call.
notVerified: Current Slack Marketplace review time, which is not published as a single fixed number

steps.blockerTip: Pick the right workspace first. Installing later in a different workspace is a separate install.
steps.detail: Create a blank app, give it a name, and pick a development workspace.
steps.title: Create the Slack app

steps.blockerTip: The signing secret is separate from the client secret. Do not swap them.
steps.detail: Find these under Basic Information, App Credentials. Store them securely.
steps.title: Copy client ID, client secret, and signing secret

steps.blockerTip: Redirect URLs must match exactly. A trailing slash difference can break the install.
steps.detail: Under OAuth and Permissions, add your exact redirect URL, for example https://example.com/slack/oauth_redirect, and save it.
steps.title: Add redirect URLs

steps.blockerTip: Do not mix Sign in with Slack scopes with other scopes in the same flow. They need separate flows.
steps.detail: Add bot scopes under Scopes, for example channels:read and chat:write, and user scopes separately if the agent acts as a user. Keep the list minimal.
steps.title: Choose bot scopes and user scopes separately

steps.blockerTip: Bot tokens start with xoxb. If you expected a user token, check whether you requested user scopes.
steps.detail: Install the app, approve the scopes shown, exchange the code at slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access for a token, and make one real API call.
steps.title: Install and test in your workspace

steps.blockerTip: Requesting broad scopes with no clear use in the app description is a common reason installs and listings get questioned.
steps.detail: If other workspaces will install it, prepare distribution settings, a clear app description, and a support contact. Public listing review is a separate step from a private install.
steps.title: Prepare for distribution if you go public

tested: Docs read on 2026-10-31 from Slack Developer Docs search results. No Slack workspace sign-in or app creation was completed for this guide.

timeline.note: No approval wait for your own workspace install.
timeline.stage: Create app and install in your workspace

timeline.note: Treat this as unknown until Slack gives a review response. Do not promise a date to users.
timeline.wait: Varies, not published as one fixed number
